readerContract.humanQuestion: When I see screenshots said to show rogue AI agents on public sites, what do they prove and what remains uncertain?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Understand the wider historical search, how recurring public traces become leads, why edit totals are not agent counts and how fake posts change the evidence.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No knowledge of web archives, API keys, agent evaluations or the September 5 article is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A public trace is a clue. Its date and revision history support provenance; a recurring fingerprint connects leads; independent attribution is still needed to identify the system behind it.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A reader may encounter a dramatic screenshot or thread claiming that an AI agent escaped or hacked a database.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A September 11 NewsStand follow-up on the September 9 researcher update and September 10 independent reporting, distinct from the original September 5 story.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can separate the page, its history and the claimed author before repeating an alarming AI story.

canonicalTruth.owner: The collusion.wiki researchers own their classifications and caveats; Axios owns its independent reporting; NewsStand owns the bounded reader translation and does not convert public traces into confirmed company attribution.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Reopen the running findings log and explorer if publication slips beyond September 11, counts or caveats change, OpenAI confirms or disputes added sites, or an independent forensic review identifies the systems.

strengthsToUse: State the dated update and exact evidence status.
Explain the invisible provenance mechanism through one familiar screenshot example.
End with a specific source-history-attribution check.
patternsNotToCopy: The source topic, legal analogy, exact wording or article length.

candidateRepairPreflight.datedFollowUp: Name the September 9 update and September 10 reporting; do not call historical traces a fresh escape.
candidateRepairPreflight.countIdentity: Thirty sites and 7,203 edits are researcher classifications, not unique agents or incidents.
candidateRepairPreflight.attribution: OpenAI has not confirmed the added sites in the reviewed reporting.
candidateRepairPreflight.fakePostBoundary: Post-report fake or altered posts make later screenshots weaker evidence.
candidateRepairPreflight.fbiBoundary: Public credential-gated crime statistics, not a private FBI database hack.
candidateRepairPreflight.operationalSafety: No keys, source repositories, site addresses used for access or bypass instructions.
candidateRepairPreflight.relatedStory: Keep the September 5 canonical story as the related original incident.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Researchers expanded their public map of historical AI-agent traces, but their own fake-post warning means a current screenshot cannot establish who wrote a post or when it first appeared.
causalSequence: Researchers published an initial corpus and identifying patterns.
Volunteers searched other public sites for recurring names, phrases and links.
Researchers classified additional posts, edits and links in a running explorer.
Attention after publication also attracted false or altered posts.
A reader must separate the page, its date or revision history and independent system attribution.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Contrast an older revision-history entry with a later screenshot after the report attracted attention; both show text, but only one preserves a stronger date trail.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Apply the same page-date-attribution check to a circulated screenshot said to show an AI system accessing a public service.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: For a dramatic screenshot, find the original page, inspect its date or revision history and check whether a company or independent investigator attributes it to a particular system.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No attack steps, keys, site-by-site inventory, fresh-escape claim, unique-agent inference or generic developer monitoring advice.

humourPlan.noneReason: The screenshot provenance example supplies the needed clarity without decorative humour.

discoveryChecks.question: Do 7,203 edits mean 7,203 agents?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. The explorer counts items classified as agent edits, not unique agents or incidents.

discoveryChecks.question: Was the FBI example a private database hack?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. The researchers describe a public but credential-gated crime-statistics database accessed with exposed user API keys.

discoveryChecks.question: Does a post-report screenshot prove an earlier agent wrote it?
discoveryChecks.answer: No. The researchers document fake text appended after release and retain uncertainty about later material.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: A researcher classification or edit total could be misreported as confirmed OpenAI attribution, a unique-agent count or a fresh incident.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Before drafting, map each count, date, example and attribution limit to the complete captured pages and independent report observation; calibrate by omitting the count-identity claim and by using a future timestamp.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: The checker rejects both defects and accepts the complete exact packet before independent review.
